items.readable_text:
Content:
Consider an absolute value graph that has undergone the following transformations:

Content:
- vertical stretch with scale factor [MATH: a]
- translation of [MATH: h] units right and [MATH: k] units up

Content:
In general, we can express the equation of this graph as

Content:
[MATH: y= a |x-h|+k.]

Content:
Note that if [MATH: a] is negative, the graph is reflected in the [MATH: x]-axis.

Content:
For example, to plot the graph of [MATH: y=-3|x-2|+1,] we proceed as follows:

Content:
- Take the graph of [MATH: y=-|x|.]
- Stretch it vertically by a scale factor of [MATH: 3] to get the graph of [MATH: y=-3|x|.]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/b085fc180ba191ec3821e79436954e29]

Content:
- Translate the result by [MATH: 2] units to the right and [MATH: 1] unit up to get the graph of [MATH: y=-3|x-2|+1.]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/ff9df1e92ae5290b062260d409289b48]

sections.normalized_html:
First, let's re-write the equation using the properties of the absolute value function:

[MATH: y|=|2x − 3|; =|2(x − (3)/(2))|; =|2|⋅|x − (3)/(2)|; = 2|x − (3)/(2)|]

Now, to get the graph of [MATH: y=2\left|x-\dfrac 3 2\right|,] we proceed as follows:

  • Take the graph of [MATH: y=|x|.]

  • Stretch it vertically by a scale factor of [MATH: 2] to get the graph of [MATH: y=2|x|.]

  • Translate the result by [MATH: \dfrac 3 2] units to the right to get the graph of [MATH: y=2\left|x-\dfrac 3 2\right|.]

items.title: Finding the Equation of a Scaled Absolute Value Function With a Translation

sections.normalized_html: Given the graph of [MATH: y=a |x|+b] below, find the value of [MATH: a+b.]
sections.readable_text:
Given the graph of [MATH: y=a |x|+b] below, find the value of [MATH: a+b.]

[IMG: /graphics/a46365496382c7bdff2e9a81d3f40079]

sections.normalized_html:
Remember that [MATH: y= a|x|+b] is a scaled absolute value graph [MATH: y=a|x|] that is translated [MATH: b] units up.

Here, the graph is moved down by [MATH: 1] unit. This corresponds to [MATH: b = -1.] So, we have

[MATH: y=a|x|-1.]

To find the value of [MATH: a,] we can pick a point on the curve and substitute it into the equation. Notice that the curve passes through the point [MATH: (1,2),] so we can substitute [MATH: x=1] and [MATH: y=2] into the equation:

[MATH: y|= a|x|− 1; 2|= a ⋅|1|− 1; 2|= a ⋅ 1 − 1; 2|= a − 1; a|= 3]

Therefore, the equation of the curve is [MATH: y=3|x|-1.]

Finally, we have [MATH: a + b = 3 + (-1) = 2.]
